about: Corrections of who holds which place in 1356, applied after the anchor-based spread (tools/map/borders.py). Each rule names its sources.

rules.note: Islands within sight of a coast belonged to the coastal power that held it; exceptions follow.
sources: W. R. Shepherd, Historical Atlas (1923), Europe about 1360

rules.note: Halogaland and Finnmark: the Norwegian crown held the coast to Varanger (Vardohus built 1307); the inland Sapmi stayed shared Sami land.
sources: K. Helle (ed.), Cambridge History of Scandinavia I (2003), ch. 15

rules.note: Orkney and Shetland: Norwegian earldoms until the pledges of 1468 and 1469.
sources: B. E. Crawford, The Northern Earldoms (2013)

rules.note: Berwick: taken by the Scots in November 1355, retaken by Edward III in January 1356. Jersey: a possession of the English crown.
sources: R. Nicholson, Scotland: The Later Middle Ages (1974), 160-163

rules.note: Hvar and Brac: Venetian 1278-1358 (lost at the Treaty of Zadar). Karpathos: the Cornaro's Venetian lordship (1306-1538).
sources: J. V. A. Fine, The Late Medieval Balkans (1987), 343-345
K. M. Setton, The Papacy and the Levant I (1976)

rules.note: Bornholm: held by the archbishop of Lund under the Danish crown; not part of the Scanian lands pledged to Magnus of Sweden in 1332.
sources: Cambridge History of Scandinavia I, ch. 14

rules.note: Transoxiana, Balkh, Termez and Shash are the western Chagatai ulus under Amir Qazaghan in 1356, not the Golden Horde's (which holds Khwarezm until c.1360) nor the Kartids' (Herat, Ghur, Badghis, Farah). Manz 1989 ch. 2; Grousset 1970 pp. 342-344
sources: B. F. Manz, The Rise and Rule of Tamerlane (1989)
R. Grousset, The Empire of the Steppes (1970)
